messages:
Alex: quick idea — proposing a 'probabilistic degrade' option in the rollout console. instead of hard switch, we gradually route a fraction to the fallback based on recent error signal distribution. keeps traffic flowing and avoids big QoS cliffs. thoughts?
Maria: interesting. how do you decide the fraction? fixed ramp vs adaptive? :thinking:
Alex: adaptive. simple heuristic: p = clamp((err_rate - base) / spread, 0, 1). err_rate is smoothed over 1m/5m windows, base is tolerated error floor. we can expose knobs or let system pick defaults.
Jon: two immediate concerns: billing attribution (who pays for tokens hitting fallback) and quotas. we must ensure quotas/limits are checked per-route even when probabilistic routing hops to fallback.
Sree: operator & audit story: must log every routing decision (sampled) with reason flags so we can replay. also need one-click freeze/override in console. otherwise ops will hate chasing ghosts.
Alex: agreed. sketching the UX: rollout panel shows a slider + an "adaptive" checkbox. when adaptive on, we show live graph: err_rate, routed_pct, predicted cost delta. clicking any point in history can open a sampled trace (click -> open trace id).
Maria: can we keep variants of degrade modes? e.g., "probabilistic-prefetch" (route early tokens to a cached shorter-model), "probabilistic-full-fallback" (route to alt-model), and "quiet-drop" (return lightweight error payload). different breadcrumbs in audit.
Alex: yes — mode enum. we'll include short labels in the UI and the audit log like `mode=alt-model, reason=latency-spike, sampled=true`.
Jon: please add a hard SLA guard: if overall success rate < X for more than Ys, auto-escalate to full fallback (not probabilistic). avoids long tail outages. also, make sure rate-limiting and quota counters use origin attribution (original route) for billing accuracy.
Sree: here's a minimal config prototype I'd want in the config API so product/infra teams can integrate: 
```yaml
rollout_id: r_1234
mode: adaptive_probabilistic
metrics:
  error_signal: p50_5m_errors
  base_threshold: 0.01
  spread: 0.05
guards:
  hard_escalation_window: 30s
  hard_escalation_threshold: 0.2
telemetry:
  sample_rate: 0.01   # fraction of routed decisions recorded in full trace
  audit_retention_days: 90
operator_controls:
  freeze_route: true
  manual_override_api: /v1/rollouts/r_1234/override
```
Maria: nice. what's the default sample_rate? 1% might be heavy for high QPS. can we do adaptive sampling too (higher when anomalous)?
Alex: propose default 0.1% for global high volume customers, 1% for mid, and adaptive spike sampling when err_rate changes by > 2x.
Jon: also need a tiny UX for cost preview prior to enabling: estimate monthly token delta given current traffic and routed_pct. show both median and 95th. Ops need predictable numbers before flipping it on.
Sree: audit fields we must capture per decision (even if sampled): timestamp, rollout_id, mode, routed_to, err_rate_snapshot, reason_flag, operator_id_if_override. btw make operator_id optional but recorded when present.
Alex: agreed. last thought: deploy-bot could post a periodic summary to channel when adaptive mode is toggled or when hard-escalation fires. low-noise digest.
deploy-bot: will post rollout summaries to #eng-platform when feature flag `prob_degrade` is turned on. format will include routing histogram + top error classifiers. :robot_face:
Maria: next step — product + design sync. i'll mock up the slider and the small trace drilldown. Alex, can you add this config prototype to the rollout-api RFC? i'll add the UX comps after that.
Alex: on it. i'll open a short RFC and tag you both. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
